title: Berneron Mirage 34 "Viridian" Chrysoprase Dial Full Set Like New
description: The Berneron Mirage debuted in 2023. This asymetrical model made an incredible impression with collectors and is synonymous with the brand. The Mirage 34 is the is the smaller iteration of the Mirage series. Sylvain Berneron never publicly sold or marketed this watch. Instead, it was only privately offered to top clients, making it the most exclusive timepiece that Berneron has ever produced. These watches are powered by the in-house calibre 215 which is beautifully displayed through the exhibition case back. The movement’s mainplate and bridges are made of 18k gold. It is a manual-wind movement with a 72 hour power reserve. The Viridian features a stunning chrysoprase dial that is unlike anything in the industry. It features curved gold hands to complement the asymmetrical case. The case measures 34mm in diameter and is made of 18k white gold. This example has been worn one time and is like new. It was sold in 2025. For those who admire the independent watchmaking spirit, Berneron is certainly the most exciting manufacturer that has emerged in the 2020s. These watches have had tremendous results recently selling at $521,400 on LoupeThis and $497,000 at Phillips . We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It comes full set with a box or papers from the original owner.

title: F.P.Journe Octa Calendrier Salmon Dial in Rose Gold  Full Set Unpolished
description: The Octa Calendrier was first introduced in 2002-2003. The model remained in production until circa 2015. The F.P.Journe Octa Calendrier is one of the most sophisticated watches and a contemporary classic wristwatch. According to the F.P.Journe, this example dates to circa 2006 when it was registered by the last owner. The watch is powered by the automatic calibre 1300.2 in 18k rose gold. It features an annual calendar with power-reserve indicator and date with a retrograde format. This is very elegant timepiece. The case appears to be unpolished. It measures 40.5mm in diameter (approximately 48mm lug to lug). It features a gorgeous salmon dial which is one of the most attractive variants on the Octa Calendrier. The watch comes full set with box and papers. It is paired on a blue F.P.Journe leather strap with 18k rose gold buckle. It comes with an additional brown F.P.Journe leather strap. The watch was serviced in 2025 and is running well. For those looking for a grail-independent timepiece, this Octa Calendrier is a remarkable option.

title: Joe DiMaggio's Patek Philippe Breguet Dial Reference 130 Chronograph in 18K YG w/ Extract
description: This remains the longest consecutive-game hitting streak in MLB history to this day! Throughout the May 15 to July 16, 1941 streak, he batted .408 with 15 home runs and 55 RBIs. Joltin’ Joe’s career started alongside the “Iron Horse” Lou Gehrig and ended alongside Micky Mantle. He operated at the intersection of two legendary Yankees eras (with Gehrig who played alongside Babe Ruth and was part of the Murderers’ Row 1927 Yankees team) and then with Mantle who of course had the legendary home run duel with his teammate Roger Maris in 1961. From 1943–1945, DiMaggio served in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II (which many cite as his prime years). DiMaggio had a lifetime batting average of .325 and accumulated 361 home runs. In 1955, DiMaggio was elected into the National Baseball Hall of Fame. In 1969, Joe DiMaggio was voted the greatest living baseball player. He famously married Marilyn Monroe in 1954 and they had a short marriage, but they rekindled their relationship years later and were reportedly close to marrying again before Monroe passed in 1962. According to the Extract from the Archives, this timepiece was produced in 1947 and was sold on December 12, 1948. The dial features beautiful hand-cut Breguet numerals which are confirmed in the Extract notes. It features the tachymeter scale demarcated for miles on the perimeter of the dial. This example features the spade hand configuration which was popular in the American market during the late 1940s. The watch is powered by the prestigious calibre 13-130 which was featured in many of the most important chronographs from Patek Philippe in this period. The case measures 33mm in diameter, and wears large at 41mm lug-to-lug. The 18k yellow gold case was produced by Emile Vichet, the Geneva master casemaker and features the Poinçon de Maître number 9. (Stainless steel reference 130s were produced by Wenger, Crossier or Dubois.) Emile Vichet produced the gold cases for the legendary Patek Philippe reference

title: Spencer Tracy's Rolex Explorer Reference 6350 w/ Waffle Dial Unpolished
description: This Rolex Explorer reference 6350 is an incredibly rare and important example from the early 1950s which belonged to American actor Spencer Tracy. This watch was worn in the 1956 movie ‘The Mountain’, an adventure film starring Spencer Tracy and Robert Wagner based on the French novel La neige en deuil. It is possibly one of the earliest product placements of a Rolex in a film. This example features an outstanding black “honeycomb” or “waffle” dial with very attractive lume. The textured Rolex dials of the 1950s are very uncommon and particularly important on Rolex sports models! It is paired on a Rolex Oyster Rivet bracelet with 64 end links dating to 1957 which we added and is period correct. The watch also comes with a Rolex strap and steel buckle which was worn on the Explorer for many years by Tracy. Linked here is a photo of Tracy wearing the watch. This example dates to circa 1953 with a 955,XXX serial It measures 36mm in diameter. The case appears to be unpolished. I’m often asked about which watches I would love to own if I could have anything. Watches like this waffle-dial Rolex Explorer 6350 is at the top of the list and the added provenance is an incredible bonus. This watch certainly belongs in the Rolex Museum collection - as it is the best of the best! To learn more about the history and evolution of the Rolex Explorer I, you can see my video and corresponding article Reference Points A Comprehensive Collector's Guide To The Rolex Explorer I . This watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history but it is running well.

title: Rolex FAP Peruvian Air Force Daytona Reference 6263

These are extremely interesting watches as we don’t often associate Daytonas with military use. This example features a 3.99M serial dating to circa 1975. The dial is very attractive. It features a replaced bezel, but has period Mark 2 pushers we found and placed on the watch. The central seconds hand is a replacement with a longer triangular tip, but is attractive. It is paired on an 78350 Oyster solid link bracelet with incorrect 557 end links, but they work well. The case has been lightly polished. It is powered by the manual-wind movement Caliber 727 made by Valjoux and is 37mm in diameter. The watch does not come with box or papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. This is a rare FAP Daytona and we are excited to be offering it for sale!

It is surmised that Rolex was finding the amount of text on the dial a bit tedious for the predecessor “porcelain dial” versions of the automatic Daytona. We believe the case is unpolished. title: Rolex GMT-Master Reference 6542 Bakelite Bezel
description: The Rolex GMT-Master reference 6542 marked the first reference in what would go onto become one of the most celebrated timepieces across all manufacturers. The timepiece became an icon within the James Bond movie Goldfinger after being worn by Honor Blackman during her portrayal of "Pussy Galore". It is an unmistakable watch and it is seen as grail watches for collectors who understand the importance of the 1950s Rolex sports catalog. This particular example is an outstanding 6542 with a spectacular dial, vivid original Bakelite bezel, and great provenance. These Bakelite bezels have a propensity for cracks and are radioactive, and as a result many were replaced with non-luminous, anodized aluminum bezels. The colors are so unique and it makes for an out of this world aesthetic. In addition to the Bakelite bezel, the dial is very well preserved and attractive. The reference 6542 dials are often known for cracking and crazing, but this example has one of the nicest dial we have seen on any reference 6542. The GMT hand has minimal lume loss, but this is expected in a sports watch over 65 years old. The case has been lightly polished, but is very attractive and full. The watch has a 398,XXX serial dating to circa late 1958. It is 38mm in diameter (48mm lug-to-lug). It is paired on what is likely its original Swiss-made Oyster rivet bracelet with super-desirable “Big Logo” clasp and 65 end links dating to 1959. It has been in an important private collection for a number of years. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 3 bar. To learn more about the Rolex GMT-Master, you can watch my ‘Reference Points: Understanding The Rolex GMT-Master' video and read the corresponding article. I selected this exact watch for inclusion in the Reference Points article and video, so that should tell you how I feel about the quality of this example.

title: Rolex "Puzzle" "Jigsaw" Day-Date Reference 128235 18K Everose Gold Full Set Unpolished
description: The Rolex Day-Date is one of the world’s most iconic wristwatches. It was introduced in 1956 and was the first watch to display the date, as well as the fully-spelled-out day of the week. This Rolex “Puzzle” Day-Date is one of the most desirable wristwatches on the planet. Introduced at the 2023 Watches & Wonders, the Rolex “Puzzle” (or “Emoji”/”Jigsaw”) was a watch that made the watch community astonished and excited. Nobody was certain whether the watch was a hoax or an authentic release from The Crown. This “Puzzle” Day-Date in rose gold is in outstanding condition. It is an incredible off catalog Rolex. It features a “Puzzle” calendar features 31 emojis and the days are inspirational words ("Happy," "Eternity," "Gratitude," "Peace," "Faith," "Love" and "Hope"). It features 10 rainbow baguette-cut sapphire hour indexes. The watch is powered by the Rolex Calibre 3255, with a 70-hour power reserve and a double quick-set day and date function. The case measures 36mm in diameter and approximately 43mm lug-to-lug. The watch is in excellent condition and appears to be unpolished. The watch recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. It comes as a “full set” with the original box and papers. It was sold in 2025. For those looking for an incredible and rare contemporary Rolex, this is a grail Day-Date.

title: Rolex Cellini King Midas Reference 4312 in 18K Yellow Gold Unpolished
description: The King Midas was the most expensive Rolex by far at retail in the 1960s and 1970s. Starting in the 1970s, Rolex changed the dial to “Cellini” instead of “Midas” in Greek on the dial. The Cellini and King Midas models are incredibly well made integrated bracelet models from Rolex that have been associated with Elvis Presley, Rihanna and others. It is said that Gérald Genta possibly designed these watches and they certainly seemed to be part of the evolution of integrated watch design that led to the Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, IWC Ingenieur 1832, and Patek Philippe Nautilus. This Rolex Cellini King Midas reference 4312 is a special timepiece in 18k yellow gold. The case is unpolished. It measures approximately 24mm in diameter. The dial on this watch is remarkable and features an ornate pyramid pattern. The bracelet is also quite amazing with a mesh/woven design that would be a fortune to replicate today. It features a 4.2M serial dating to circa 1976. The bracelet is quite long and will fit a wrist over 7.5 inches. It has likely never been cut. For those looking for a stylish and unique Rolex, this is an incredible choice. The watch does not come with box and papers. We do not know the service history, but it is running well.

The reference 127234 is beautiful 36mm case with one of the most comfortable bracelets. The watch is powered by the Rolex automatic calibre 7135 which is seen in the exhibition caseback. This example is unpolished. It features the beautiful honeycomb dial motif, and the 6 and 9 numerals inspired by the 1950s Rolex dials. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does comes full set with box and papers from the original owner. It was sold in 2025.

title: Rolex Tropical Double Red Sea-Dweller Reference 1665 Thin Case
description: This Rolex Sea-Dweller reference 1665 features the highly desired and vibrant "Double Red" dial and the rare thin case. The earliest Sea-Dwellers such as this example used cases like on the Rolex Submariner reference 5512, but with a helium escape valve (HEV) added to the left side of the case. The case is lightly polished, but in strong condition overall. The watch measures 40mm in diameter. It previously came from the original owner. The amazing tropical dial has the original tritium lume on the dial and hands. The aluminum bezel insert has faded to a beautiful grey color. The watch features a 1.7 million serial with inside case back dating to circa 1967. These were not assembled by Rolex to be Sea-Dwellers until later. The watch came from the original owner who purchased it new in New Zealand in the early 1970s. The gentleman’s wife was upset about the cost of the watch, but it was already purchased. The gentleman was a roofer and did various forms of manual labor. One day, he was on a roof and he took his watch off and left it on the roof so it would not get damaged while he was working. Unfortunately, he slipped and fell off the roof. He went to the hospital for a few days and when he regained his senses he realized his Rolex was probably still on the roof. He went back about a week later once he had left the hospital and promptly climbed onto the roof to find his watch still sitting there. He joked that spending the week in the sun up on the roof might have helped the dial turn “tropical” brown. The watch does not come with box and papers. Overall, this is an amazing opportunity to get a spectacular and rare Rolex sports watch. We do not know the service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar.

This watch was originally issued to Merwin Stanley “Stan” Follis who was issued the watch by the Navy when he joined the video branch of the Naval Electronics Laboratory Center after graduating from USC with a bachelor’s degree and master’s degree in cinema. Stan passed away earlier this year at the age of 92 after a successful career and the watch came from his estate. It is a miraculous find and a sort of American MilSub.

title: Patek Philippe Retailed by Brock & Co. Reference 42 Tank in 18K White Gold w/ Extract
description: This is an incredibly special rectangular timepiece from Patek Philippe dating to 1927. The watch is an early wristwatch produced in a time when the primary exports in Switzerland were pocket watches. The wristwatch would eventually become more prominent for Patek Philippe by the early 1930s. This example is a very rare model that was produced for the Beverly Hills based retailer Brock & Co. There are a handful of Patek Philippe wristwatches for Brock & Co of this era. Examples from this period include the references 42 and 425 made of gold or platinum. The designs of these watches were reminiscent of the trend-setting Cartier Tank. The Tank had been released about decade prior, and the Art Deco styles defined the watch industry throughout the 1920s. The dial features an incredible two-tone sector dial with the “Cat Whiskers” hour markers (2, 4, 8, and 9 o’clock). Both the manufactuer and retailer signature are engraved hard enamel. The case is made of 18k white gold. It measures approximately 33mm in length by 25mm in diameter. It has been lightly polished. The case design is quite incredible, as it is reminiscent of the pocket watches and features a hinged case at 12 o’clock. The watch is powered by the manual wind calibre 9 movement with lever escapement. We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. It does not come with a box or papers. The watch comes with an Extract from the Archives.

The reference 3147 was the first Heuer Carrera with date and this is a 3147N with the N meaning “Noir” indicating a black dial. The movement is a Landeron 189 with date and the case back is thicker on these to accommodate the thicker movement with the date. The case diameter is 36mm with a lug width of 18mm. The present example is a bit of a hodgepodge. The watch features service replacement hands with Super-LumiNova. The case has been lightly polished and it has a replacement crystal. The case back sticker is in tact. It is possible the dial was placed in the watch. Regardless, it is a very rare dial and highly coveted vintage Heuer. An Autavia model with this dial sold at Christie’s for nearly $200,000 back in 2017 . You can read more about the origins of the Carrera in the in-depth article that I wrote for HODINKEE back in 2013 . We do not know the service history, but the watch is running well. title: Universal Genève Dato-Compax Reference 22325 W/ WWII Provenance Unpolished
description: This is more than just a spectacular Universal Geneve Dato-Compax chronograph. It was Mayhew Y. "Bo" Foster's timekeeper on May 9, 1945 while he flew Hermann Göring in a Stinson L-5 Sentinel from Kitzbuhel, Austria to Augsburg, Germany for interrogation by the 7th Army before he later stood trial at Nuremberg. “Bo" Foster (October 9, 1911 – March 21, 2011) was a decorated American pilot and hero. Foster graduated in 1937 with a degree in English from Yale. For his actions in World War II - including 70 reconnaissance combat missions - Foster was awarded the Silver Star for his service in France in 1944, the Air Medal, and the Légion d'Honneur for his contribution to liberating France. Foster later reached the rank of Brigadier General in the Montana Army National Guard Foster transported Göring in the L-5, a larger plane than the L-4 he normally piloted, because Göring weighed more than 300 pounds. In a letter to his wife, Virginia, written at the time, Foster described his first impression of Göring as "effeminate [and he] gave me the creeps . . . Several times I had the impulse to turn the plane over and see if I could shake him out, but he was wedged in like a champagne cork… He acted as though he was going on a sightseeing tour, or really as though I was going on a sightseeing tour, and he was showing me where he grew up. I had a .45 in a shoulder holster, but he couldn't reach that. But neither could I, because I had two hands controlling the plane.” When Foster arrived, there was just a single jeep at the airstrip to meet the arriving flight. Foster rode with Göring and formally turned him over to the intelligence officer without ceremony. It seems likely that Göring was also wearing a Universal Geneve chronograph in steel on that flight - in his case an oversized non-luminous Compax reference 22430 that was in his possession at Nuremberg and sold at auction in 2016. The dial is decorated by Rolex with the Panama Canal in substitution of the depth rating. These special dial Rolex models have been discontinued many years ago, but there is a rich history of special dials for corporations including the Rolex Domino's Air-Kings, Rolex Coca-Cola Oyster Perpetuals, and many more. This example is an incredible case and bracelet are made of 18k rose gold (6N) which is incredibly comfortable and elegant on the wrist. F.P.Journe collectors love these bracelets and they are among the best quality in the industry. The case and bracelet feature the “hammered” finish which is an attractive matte finish which is much more attractive than other manufacturers. The case measures approximately 42mm in diameter. The dial features non-luminous matte 5N Gold applied numerals. It features whitened guilloché subdials in silver with red accents. These grey dial variants were recently discontinued and transitioned to a black dial variant, making this one of the final grey variants. The movement is an engineering highlight. It is powered by the calibre 1506 - a movement which is made of titanium and weighs approximately 12 grams. The lineSport Centigraphe Reference CT2 is arguably one of the most advanced chronograph models ever produced capable of timing one-hundredth of a second. The subdials feature a 1/100th of a second at 10 o'clock, a 20 second dial, and a 10-minute dial at 6 o'clock. The watch comes full set from the original owner. It is in brand new condition. title: Rolex Domino's Air-King 14000 Full Set W/ Hangtag Unpolished
description: The Rolex-Domino’s connection is perhaps the ultimate high-low collaboration. These watches were not made for purchase by the public, but as a way to reward Domino’s franchise owners who hit their sales targets. All these watches were originally ordered through Schlanderer and Sons in Ann Arbor, Michigan, where Domino’s has its headquarters. In the past, these watches on the secondhand market were generally the least expensive Rolex a person could purchase as few people wanted a pizza logo like this on their dial. Dealers would buy them, swap out the Domino’s dial, and polish off the case back initials. Over the last year, however, they have gained a massive following. The watch features an engraving on the back with the recipient’s initials. You can learn about these watches in our video Collector Conversation: Tom Monaghan - Founder of Domino's Pizza - on the Domino's Rolex . This version features the “tilted logo” that is the last version of Dominos’s Rolex watch with the logo on the dial. . The watch features a U^ serial dating to 1997. The case appears to be unpolished. The watch comes as a “full set” with a box, papers and hangtag. It was originally sold in 1998. We do not know the full service history, but it is running well. It recently passed a water resistance test of 5 bar. To learn more about Rolex-Domino’s story, watch the video ”Rolex Model NEVER in Stores” . This watch is available through J. Press.
